title: Anna Anderson insisted she was Grand Duchess Anastasia Romanov.
description:
Anna Anderson insisted she was Grand Duchess Anastasia Romanov. She surfaced in Germany in 1920, after a suicide attempt, and never once dropped the story.

How long Anderson held to the claim, from 1920 until her death in 1984.

DNA from Anderson's own body did not match a single Romanov. Tested from a tissue sample kept after a 1979 operation, and hair found in her late husband's book.

A relative of Franziska Schanzkowska, the Polish factory worker Anderson really was. His DNA matched Anderson's exactly, closing the case.

The myth had somewhere real to hide. Two Romanov children's remains were not found until 2007.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna_Anderson: confirms Anna Anderson was born Franziska Schanzkowska on 16 December 1896, surfaced in Germany in 1920 claiming to be Grand Duchess Anastasia after being institutionalised following a suicide attempt, died on 12 February 1984 in Charlottesville, Virginia, and records that DNA testing used a tissue sample kept from a 1979 operation plus hair found in a book belonging to her husband Jack Manahan; the mitochondrial DNA from both matched Karl Maucher, a relative of Franziska Schanzkowska, and did not match the Romanov remains found in 1991 or living Romanov relatives.
- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2652717/: a 2009 peer reviewed paper confirming that the remains of the final two Romanov children, Alexei and Maria, were not discovered until the summer of 2007 near Yekaterinburg, decades after the rest of the family's remains were found in 1991, and that DNA analysis was used to identify them.
